# Story 10 — Customer Portal

## Prerequisites

- `knowledge-base` feature completed: published FAQ / article content and search must exist for the portal to list.
- `tickets` feature completed: `TicketService`, `TicketComment.IsInternal`, `TicketService.GetCommentsAsync(id, includeInternal)`, `TicketsController` all in place.
- `customers` feature completed: `Customer.UserId`, `ApplicationUser.CustomerId`, `CustomerNote.IsInternal`, and customer attachment endpoints exist.
- `channels` feature completed: `CommunicationChannel.Portal` enum value and `InboundMessageProcessor` / `OutboundDispatcher` wiring so a portal reply behaves as a normal outbound reply.
- `reports` feature planned: this story only writes CSAT rows; aggregation is that story's problem.
- Coordinate with owners of `Application/Auth/Roles.cs`, `Application/Auth/Permissions.cs`, and `Api/Auth/PermissionAuthorization.cs` — a new **Portal** authorization policy is added here.

---

## Story Goal

Deliver a **customer-facing portal** — a separate URL space in the same Vue application and a separate `/api/portal/**` surface in the same ASP.NET Core API — that lets an authenticated customer:

1. Register (or accept an invite), verify email, sign in, and reset a forgotten password. The login is linked to exactly one `Customer` row via the existing `Customer.UserId` / `ApplicationUser.CustomerId` pair.
2. Submit a new ticket (with attachments and a category), see the ticket number, and reply on the public thread.
3. Track ticket status, read the **public** reply thread (no internal notes, no staff-only fields), and browse full request history.
4. Browse and search published FAQ / knowledge-base articles.
5. Rate a resolved ticket (CSAT) exactly once with an optional comment.

**Non-goals** (explicitly out of scope for this story):

- The AI chatbot itself (belongs to `ai-features`).
- Aggregated satisfaction dashboards (`reports`).
- Social / SSO login.
- Reusing staff DTOs with conditional field-stripping — the portal must have its **own** controllers and DTOs so internal fields cannot leak.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** every API endpoint and every frontend route today serves a staff persona; `Roles.Customer` exists in code but has no surface.
- **New behaviour:** portal endpoints live under `/api/portal/**`, are guarded by a new `PortalOnly` policy that requires the `Roles.Customer` role, and are hard-scoped by the caller's `CustomerId` claim.

### 4 — Portal application services

**Create file:** `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Application/Portal/PortalTicketService.cs`

- Depends on `IAppDbContext`, `ICurrentUser`, `IClock`, `IReferenceNumberGenerator`, `IFileStorage`.
- Every query starts with `.Where(t => t.CustomerId == _currentUser.CustomerId!.Value)`. Fetch by id returns `null` → throw `NotFoundException` (never `ForbiddenException`, so ids cannot be probed).
- `CreateAsync(PortalCreateTicketRequest)`:

- `AddReplyAsync(Guid ticketId, PortalReplyRequest)`:
  - Wraps `TicketService.AddCommentAsync` with `IsInternal = false` **hard-coded**.

- `RateAsync(Guid ticketId, PortalRateRequest)`:
  - Only allowed when `Status` is a terminal / resolved status per `TicketWorkflow`.
  - Score must be 1–5.
  - Uniqueness enforced by DB unique index (see migration below) plus a pre-check that throws `ConflictException` on duplicate.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Foreign-ticket probe** — `GET /api/portal/tickets/{id}` where the ticket belongs to another customer. Trigger: any customer supplies a guessed id. Expected: `404 Not Found`. Enforced in `PortalTicketService.GetByIdAsync` by combining the id filter with `CustomerId == _currentUser.CustomerId` in the same LINQ query, then throwing `NotFoundException` on null.
- **Serialised-payload leak** — a future refactor that reuses a staff DTO would leak `AssignedAgentId` etc. Mitigation: portal DTOs live in a separate namespace and the leak test (see Test Plan #4) asserts on the JSON keys returned.
- **Duplicate rating** — Trigger: second `POST /rating` on the same ticket. Expected: `409 Conflict`. Enforced by the unique index on `TicketSatisfaction.TicketId` **and** an explicit pre-check that throws `ConflictException`.
- **Rating an unresolved ticket** — Expected: `400 Bad Request`. Enforced in `PortalTicketService.RateAsync` by checking `TicketWorkflow` terminal states.
- **Email enumeration on register** — Trigger: attacker POSTs `register` with a known email. Expected: same success shape as a fresh registration; the email that goes out to the existing user simply notifies them of the attempted signup. Enforced in `PortalAuthService.RegisterAsync`.
- **Email enumeration on password reset** — Trigger: `POST /forgot-password` with an unknown email. Expected: `200 OK` with the same body as a real reset. Enforced in `PortalAuthService.RequestPasswordResetAsync`.
- **Deactivated account** — Trigger: `ApplicationUser` marked disabled / soft-deleted. Expected: login refused, and any existing JWT rejected on next call. Enforced by adding an `ITokenValidator` check on user active-status in the JWT bearer events (or by having `PortalOnly` handler re-check the user on each request — pick one and document).
- **Missing `customer_id` claim** — Trigger: a `Roles.Customer` user without a linked `Customer`. Expected: `403 Forbidden` from `PortalOnly` policy handler. Enforced in `PortalAuthorizationHandler`.
- **Staff user hits `/api/portal/**`** — Expected: `403 Forbidden` (policy requires role `Customer`). Enforced by `[Authorize(Policy = "PortalOnly")]` on every portal controller.
- **Customer user hits any staff endpoint** — Expected: `403 Forbidden`. Enforced by existing `[Authorize(Roles = Roles.Staff)]` / policy on those controllers; verified by a smoke test.
- **Rate limit trip on `/api/portal/auth/**`** — Trigger: >20 requests/min from one IP. Expected: `429 Too Many Requests`. Enforced by `portal-anon` limiter policy.
- **Attachment size / MIME** — Trigger: oversized or disallowed file. Expected: `400`. Reuse existing `IFileStorage` guards.
- **Concurrent reply + status change** — Trigger: agent closes ticket while customer submits a reply. Expected: reply succeeds when workflow allows a comment on the current status; otherwise `409`. Enforced by `TicketWorkflow` in `TicketService.AddCommentAsync`.
- **Locale switch** — Trigger: customer toggles ar/en. Expected: `<html lang>` and `<html dir>` update via `ui` store; page mirrors correctly with logical properties.
- **375px viewport** — Manually resize the browser to 375px; no horizontal scroll on any portal view.

   1. Staff-role caller on `/api/portal/tickets` → 403.
   2. Customer-role caller on `/api/tickets` (staff) → 403.
   3. Anonymous caller on `/api/portal/tickets` → 401.
   4. Customer-role caller without `customer_id` claim → 403.
6. **Frontend locale spec:** `frontend/src/locales/locales.spec.ts` — no change to the test itself; it will automatically catch any missing key parity between `ar.json` and `en.json` in the new `portal.*` namespace.

---

## Migration / Rollback

- Migration `PortalCsatUniqueIndex` adds a **unique index** on `TicketSatisfaction.TicketId`.
- Pre-check: run a `SELECT TicketId, COUNT(*) FROM TicketSatisfactions GROUP BY TicketId HAVING COUNT(*) > 1` on production before applying. Deduplicate (keep earliest) if any duplicates exist; the unique index will otherwise fail to create.
- Rollback: `dotnet ef migrations remove` and drop the index manually. No data is destroyed.
- Half-applied state: safe — the new controllers refuse requests unless the DB is on the migration; if the DB is rolled back, the app fails on `RateAsync` at write time with a normal EF exception rather than data corruption.

---

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** `dotnet build backend/CustomerSupportCRM.slnx`
2. **Backend tests:** `dotnet test backend/CustomerSupportCRM.slnx` — all existing + new tests pass.
3. **Migration applies:**
   ```bash
   dotnet ef database update \
     --project backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure \
     --startup-project backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api
   ```
4. **Frontend builds:** `npm run build --prefix frontend`
5. **Frontend runs:** `npm run dev --prefix frontend` and API `dotnet run --project backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api`.
6. **Smoke — happy path (staff still works):** sign in as seeded admin at `/login`; open a ticket list; nothing regresses.
7. **Smoke — portal happy path:** register a customer at `/portal/register`; confirm email (log-scraped token in dev); sign in at `/portal/login`; create a ticket; add a reply; when an agent (other window) resolves it, rate it 5 stars.
8. **Smoke — leak checks:** using browser devtools, inspect the JSON body of `GET /api/portal/tickets/{id}` and confirm no internal fields.
9. **Smoke — cross-role denial:** while signed in as staff, `GET /api/portal/tickets` → 403; while signed in as customer, `GET /api/tickets` → 403.
10. **Smoke — probe protection:** while signed in as customer A, `GET /api/portal/tickets/{customerBTicketId}` → **404** (not 403).
11. **Regression — locale parity:** `npm test --prefix frontend` (or the specific `locales.spec.ts`) passes.
12. **Regression — responsive:** open Chrome devtools, set viewport to 375×667, walk every portal view; no horizontal scroll.
13. **Regression — RTL:** switch to Arabic; confirm layout mirrors and ticket numbers keep LTR digit order (`.ltr-nums`).
14. **Regression — rate limit:** hit `POST /api/portal/auth/login` 25 times in 60s from one IP; expect 429s after the limit.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] Customer can register, verify email, sign in, and reset a forgotten password; login is linked to exactly one `Customer` row via `Customer.UserId` / `ApplicationUser.CustomerId`.
- [ ] `GET /api/portal/tickets/{id}` for another customer's ticket returns **404** (verified by `GetByIdAsync_ForeignTicket_Throws_NotFound_NotForbidden`).
- [ ] Portal responses omit every internal / staff-only field (verified by `PortalDtoLeakTests`).
- [ ] Customer can submit a ticket with attachments and a category and receives the generated ticket number.
- [ ] Customer can track status, read the public thread, reply, and browse full history via `/portal/tickets`.
- [ ] Customer can browse and search published FAQ / KB articles at `/portal/faq`.
- [ ] Customer can rate a resolved ticket **once**; second attempt returns 409.
- [ ] Portal has its own layout (`PortalLayout.vue`) and route tree (`/portal/**`), fully bilingual (all strings under `portal.*` in `ar.json` and `en.json`), RTL-mirrored, responsive at 375px.
- [ ] `/api/portal/auth/**` is rate-limited by the `portal-anon` policy; a customer JWT cannot access any `/api/**` staff endpoint.
- [ ] Deactivated customer cannot sign in and an existing token is rejected.
- [ ] `dotnet build`, `dotnet test`, and `npm run build --prefix frontend` all pass.
